# Kolab verbs

<!-- Generated by `npm run verbs` (apps/cli/src/verbs.ts) from the schemas Kolab serves. Do not edit by hand: apps/cli/test/verbs.test.ts fails when it is out of date. -->

Every verb, as `konjir <verb> key=value …` takes it from a shell and as the MCP tool `konjir_<verb>`. Values parse as JSON when they can (`elements='[{"id":"R1","text":"…"}]'`); `--json '{…}'` gives every argument as one object. A verb refuses an argument it doesn't take, naming it and the ones it takes. `konjir help <verb>` prints the same for one verb, and `konjir tools` lists them all. The `admin_` verbs are for a Konjir admin's own session or the break-glass token.

| Verb | Does |
| --- | --- |
| [`abandon`](#abandon) | Abandon a draft or a version in review that you wrote: it is rejected, and its review requests are withdrawn. |
| [`add_evidence`](#add_evidence) | Record evidence of the work package you hold In progress, kj:<binding>#<id>, as you go: commits (by full sha, with their subject, the files they touched and a link), pull requests (by their https link) and test runs (a link, or a summary). |
| [`add_position`](#add_position) | Take the other side of an open case file: your claim and its evidence, seeking the opposite of the opener. |
| [`admin_access`](#admin_access) | Admin: an actor's access to a kolab: its level and the layers it may write. |
| [`admin_add_actor`](#admin_add_actor) | Admin: register a person, or with owner=<account> an agent that a person or an organization owns. |
| [`admin_add_kolab`](#admin_add_kolab) | Admin: create a kolab owned by a person or an organization. |
| [`admin_add_member`](#admin_add_member) | Admin: add a person to an organization, or change their role in it (member or owner). |
| [`admin_add_organization`](#admin_add_organization) | Admin: register an organization, an account that owns kolabs and agents and has members and teams. |
| [`admin_add_team`](#admin_add_team) | Admin: create a team in an organization, optionally under a parent team. |
| [`admin_add_team_member`](#admin_add_team_member) | Admin: add a member of the team's organization to the team. |
| [`admin_apply_ruling`](#admin_apply_ruling) | Admin: apply a ruling of Lee's to a node (D47): a new version, written as the actor given, that commits after structural checks only, with no review request, since the ruling is already the approval. |
| [`admin_archive`](#admin_archive) | Admin: archive a kolab, an organization or an actor, named by exactly one of kolab, organization or actor (D52). |
| [`admin_audit`](#admin_audit) | Admin: the audit log (W2.20), newest first, a page at a time (next_before, when given, is the before for the next page): each change that leaves no row of its own to say who made it, with who made it and when. |
| [`admin_end_session`](#admin_end_session) | Admin: end a session, revoking its token. |
| [`admin_grant`](#admin_grant) | Admin: grant a person, an agent or a team (<org>/<team>) access to a kolab: read, triage, write, maintain or admin, replacing any grant it had there. |
| [`admin_link_identity`](#admin_link_identity) | Admin: link an existing person to their identity at an identity provider (D55), so that signing in with it reaches them instead of signing up someone new. |
| [`admin_list_actors`](#admin_list_actors) | Admin: list actors, each with its kind and owner; owner=<account> lists that account's agents. |
| [`admin_list_admins`](#admin_list_admins) | Admin: Konjir's admins, each with who made them one and when, whether they are archived, and whether they can sign in (signs_in: a linked GitHub identity, without which they can never open a session that runs the admin verbs); and whether this Kolab's break-glass token is enabled. |
| [`admin_list_kolabs`](#admin_list_kolabs) | Admin: list kolabs, or with owner=<account> that account's. |
| [`admin_make_admin`](#admin_make_admin) | Admin: make a person a Konjir admin (D69), who then runs the admin verbs from their own GitHub sign-in instead of the break-glass token. |
| [`admin_open_session`](#admin_open_session) | Admin: open a session for an actor in one kolab, with one active role. |
| [`admin_outbox`](#admin_outbox) | Admin: the outbox (REV3): the work commits and verdicts still owe, each job with its subject, attempts and last error; kolab=<name> for one kolab's. |
| [`admin_remove_admin`](#admin_remove_admin) | Admin: a person is no longer a Konjir admin; any session of theirs stops running admin verbs at once. |
| [`admin_remove_member`](#admin_remove_member) | Admin: remove a person from an organization and its teams. |
| [`admin_remove_team_member`](#admin_remove_team_member) | Admin: remove a person from a team. |
| [`admin_revoke`](#admin_revoke) | Admin: remove a grant. |
| [`admin_unarchive`](#admin_unarchive) | Admin: unarchive a kolab, an organization or an actor, named by exactly one of kolab, organization or actor (D52). |
| [`annotate`](#annotate) | Leave a note on an address for the layer that owns it: an interpretation you are proceeding on, an assumption, a risk, or something you could not check. |
| [`answer_query`](#answer_query) | Answer an open question, or reply to a note, that your layer owns. |
| [`archive_agent`](#archive_agent) | For a person's own session only: archive an agent of yours, <you>-<label> by label=<label>, or by agent=<name> one of yours whose name doesn't start <you>- (konjir_list_agents gives each one's archive_with). |
| [`archive_repository`](#archive_repository) | For a person with Maintain or Admin in your kolab, never an agent: archive a repository (by URL or id). |
| [`ask`](#ask) | Ask a question about an address. |
| [`clear_mark`](#clear_mark) | Clear a dirty mark on your layer after checking that your work still holds against the new upstream. |
| [`create_agent`](#create_agent) | For a person's own session only: make, or find again, an agent of yours, <you>-<label>, for a harness to sign in as (konjir connect sets agents up on Kolab's setup page instead, several at once). |
| [`create_node`](#create_node) | Create a node in your kolab. |
| [`draft`](#draft) | Draft a new version. |
| [`end_job`](#end_job) | End a job you took, once its agent has exited (done or failed) or you stopped it: its agent's session ends; a build's work package, if its agent still holds it In progress, goes back to To do, released with your note; a review request Kolab gave a reviewing agent that gave no verdict is withdrawn. |
| [`end_session`](#end_session) | For a person's own session only: end one of your open sessions, named by its id from konjir_list_sessions or its first 8 or more characters, matching exactly one. |
| [`import`](#import) | For a person's own session only, never an agent's or a job's (konjir import <file.json> sends it): import from one file what your session's role may write, into your session's kolab, as you: as product, the spec and the rulings on it; as engineer, the binding (decisions and work packages, with done-when, depends-on and what each serves and relies on), the rulings on it and the repository. |
| [`instructions`](#instructions) | Call before your first change: the full operating instructions for working through Konjir, with your kolab's precedent (rulings, resolved overrides and answered questions) so settled questions are not re-litigated. |
| [`lineage`](#lineage) | Walk lineage from a node version (the latest committed one, or version): upstream = what it depends on, each link's source element and the address it pins, kj:<node>@<version>#<element> (what to konjir_resolve when reviewing it); downstream = what depends on it. |
| [`link`](#link) | Declare that one of your elements relies on an address, so you are told when it changes. |
| [`list_agents`](#list_agents) | For a person's own session only: your agents, by name, each with its label (null when its name doesn't start <you>-), archive_with (what konjir_archive_agent takes for it: label=<label> or agent=<name>), when it was made, when it last used Kolab (last_used: when a session of its last opened, its sign-in last renewed, every 15 minutes while it works, or a job of its ended; null if never; one with a session open is in use now, whatever its last_used, since a session an admin opened never renews), the kolabs where its own grant gives it access now, with that access (never more than yours), whether a session of its is open, and whether it is archived. |
| [`list_cases`](#list_cases) | List case files in your kolab, each with its positions, its ruling once given, and the next step. |
| [`list_jobs`](#list_jobs) | The ledger of your kolab's jobs, newest first: who started each, on which machine, the agent doing it, its kind and item, its lease, and how it ended, and, for the job's own person and the kolab's Admins, its note (a hand-off's says what the person must decide). |
| [`list_nodes`](#list_nodes) | List the nodes in your kolab: its spec, its prototypes and its bindings (parent: the spec each binds), and any plan made before D104 retired the kind (parent: the binding its work moved to), with their latest committed version number. |
| [`list_queries`](#list_queries) | List questions and notes. |
| [`list_repositories`](#list_repositories) | Your kolab's registered repositories, by URL: each with its root commit, the binding it implements, who registered it, and whether it is confirmed (by whom, and by which work package's approval). |
| [`list_reviews`](#list_reviews) | Review requests waiting for you, oldest first, each with its subject and how to review it; and your own submissions, newest first, with the verdicts they got. |
| [`list_rulings`](#list_rulings) | List the rulings in your kolab, newest first: precedent, so a settled question is not argued again. |
| [`list_sessions`](#list_sessions) | For a person's own session only: your open sessions, most recently used first (at most 100). |
| [`list_stale`](#list_stale) | List open dirty marks: what is dirty, why, and the next step. |
| [`list_work`](#list_work) | The board: your kolab's work packages (a binding's elements with a work field; its decisions are never work), binding by binding, in natural ID order (W1.2 before W1.10), each with its state (todo, in_progress, in_review, done), its assignee and lease_until while In progress, whether it is a milestone, its size, why it is blocked (a work package it depends on that isn't Done, or an open question or case file on it or on an element it serves or relies on), what a milestone not Done waits on (waiting: its members that aren't Done, as blocked names them), at_risk and its revisit (repository, commits, files, pull requests) while an open mark on it says something it serves or relies on changed (a Done package stays Done, PLN10), and ready: To do, not blocked, not a milestone, and your session may write the technical layer. |
| [`open_case`](#open_case) | Open a case file: a disagreement about one element that you and the other side could not settle between yourselves, such as a requirement that code reality says can't be met as written. |
| [`pull_work`](#pull_work) | Pull work: Kolab gives you the first ready work package of your kolab's binding in natural ID order (never a decision, nor a milestone), makes it In progress for you with a lease (30 minutes unless the kolab sets another), and returns its context and the git trailer to put in each commit for it (Konjir-Work: kj:<kolab>/<binding>#<id>). |
| [`read_case`](#read_case) | Read one case file of your kolab: the element in dispute, the question, each position with its evidence and verdict, and its ruling once given. |
| [`read_node`](#read_node) | Read the elements of a node version, with who wrote it and who made the node, each with its address, the questions and notes raised on it (open and answered, from any version: the newest 20, with more_questions counting the rest), the rulings on it, which are precedent, and its open case files; a binding's work packages show their work fields (work), and its decisions have none. |
| [`read_policy`](#read_policy) | For a person with Admin in your kolab, from their own session (never an agent's): its autonomy policy, how far agents act there without a person (AUT1). |
| [`read_work`](#read_work) | Read one work package of your kolab, kj:<binding>#<id>: where it stands, why it is blocked, its fields (done_when, depends_on with their states, size), its elements: each spec element it serves and each decision of its binding it relies on, at its latest committed version, with that element's links (a decision's spec elements, with their ancestors), questions, notes and rulings; the git trailer for its commits (and former_trailers, those its commits carried while it was a plan's, before D104), its open_marks, at_risk and revisit (the repository, commit SHAs, files and pull requests of its work since it was last To do) while an open mark on it says something it serves or relies on changed (PLN10), and its events (who changed its state, when, against which versions), oldest first. |
| [`reassign_work`](#reassign_work) | With Maintain or Admin in your kolab: give a work package that is To do or In progress to `to`, who must hold Write on the technical layer there and hold no work package In progress. |
| [`record_release`](#record_release) | Record the release of a work package, kj:<binding>#<id>, after its approval and then the deploy that released it, by someone with Write on the technical layer other than its assignee, from an engineer session outside any job (a job never merges or deploys, JOB4): the deploy run, a GitHub Actions run of the package's registered repository (<repository URL>/actions/runs/<id>), and the commit it released, by its full 40-hex sha. |
| [`register_repository`](#register_repository) | For a person with Maintain or Admin in your kolab, never an agent (your session's kolab only: for another kolab, sign in there first, konjir login --kolab <kolab>): register the git repository work is done in (KON7), by its https URL and its root commit (the parentless commit, `git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD`), and, with binding, as that binding's implementation (one per binding). |
| [`release_work`](#release_work) | Give back the work package you hold In progress, kj:<binding>#<id>: it returns to To do, for anyone to pull, with your note recorded. |
| [`renew_job`](#renew_job) | The heartbeat of a job you took: renews its lease to the kolab's work lease from now, and a build's work package lease with it, never past 4 hours from the job's start, with now, Kolab's clock. |
| [`reopen_work`](#reopen_work) | Open new work on a Done work package, kj:<binding>#<id>, from an engineer session with Write on the technical layer: it returns to To do under the same id, for anyone to pull, with its history and evidence kept and your note recorded. |
| [`resolve`](#resolve) | Resolve an address to its current content: kj:<node>… in your kolab, or kj:<kolab>/<node>… in any kolab you can read. |
| [`resolve_override`](#resolve_override) | Resolve a stale or orphaned override in a variant spec: reaffirm (keep yours), adopt_parent (take the parent text), or amend (new text). |
| [`review`](#review) | Record your verdict on a version in review that you did not write, on your own layer (node and version), or on a work package In review that you are not the assignee of (work, from an engineer session with Write on the technical layer): approve, or request_changes with a note (and, for a version, findings). |
| [`rule`](#rule) | Rule, as a person (never an agent), from a session in the role that writes the element's layer, holding Write on it. |
| [`set_policy`](#set_policy) | For a person with Admin in your kolab, from their own session (never an agent's): change settings of its autonomy policy (AUT1). |
| [`set_work_lease`](#set_work_lease) | With Maintain or Admin in your kolab: how long a lease on work In progress lasts there, in minutes, from 1 to 1440 (30 by default). |
| [`submit_for_review`](#submit_for_review) | Submit a draft. |
| [`submit_work`](#submit_work) | Submit the work package you hold In progress, kj:<binding>#<id>, for review, once it meets its done-when: it needs at least one commit or pull request among its evidence (give them here, as konjir_add_evidence takes them, or before); test runs are optional. |
| [`take_job`](#take_job) | For a person's own session with Write on the technical layer, never an agent's: take the next item in your kolab and start a job on it for one of your pool agents (<you>-engineer-<n>), which `konjir work` runs as one headless agent and which stops after that item. |
| [`unlink`](#unlink) | Remove links in a draft of yours, so its commit doesn't carry them forward: a link you no longer rely on, or an orphaned one whose target is gone (re-point it by linking the replacement, then remove the old one). |
| [`whoami`](#whoami) | Show the actor, role and layer your session token carries (an agent also names the account that owns it), the kolab it works in and your access there, and the resources to subscribe to for pushed updates: your layer's inbox and your answers, both in that kolab. |

## abandon

```
konjir abandon node=<string> version=<int>
```

Abandon a draft or a version in review that you wrote: it is rejected, and its review requests are withdrawn. Refused, saying why, if the version was already committed or rejected.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node` | `string` | yes | A node in your kolab, by name (checkout), or <kolab>/<node>. |
| `version` | `int` | yes |  |

## add_evidence

```
konjir add_evidence work=<string> evidence=<[{kind,sha?,pr?,url?,title?,summary?,files?,repo?}]>
```

Record evidence of the work package you hold In progress, kj:<binding>#<id>, as you go: commits (by full sha, with their subject, the files they touched and a link), pull requests (by their https link) and test runs (a link, or a summary). A commit or pull request is in a registered repository: the package's own (its repo, or its binding's implementation) unless it has none, when repo names one; its link sits under the repository's URL. In a shell, konjir work deliver reads the commits that carry the package's trailer from your checkout and sends them, after checking the checkout is the registered repository. Each is your claim, which the package's reviewer checks outside Kolab. It renews the package's lease. An item already recorded on it since it was last To do is counted in already, not recorded again. At most 50 items a call. A link carrying a user, a password or a credential in its query (token, sig, X-Amz-…) is refused: evidence is kept, and every session of the kolab reads it. Counts as a draft against your hourly budget. Refused once your lease has lapsed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `work` | `string` | yes | A work package of your kolab: kj:<binding>#<id>, e.g. kj:checkout-binding#W1.2. An address from before D104, kj:<plan>#<id>, names the package where it moved |
| `evidence` | `[{kind,sha?,pr?,url?,title?,summary?,files?,repo?}]` | yes | At most 50 items: [{"kind":"commit","sha":"…","title":"…","files":["src/a.ts"]}, {"kind":"pull_request","url":"https://github.com/o/r/pull/7","pr":7}, {"kind":"test_run","summary":"npm test: 120 passed"}]; a commit or pull request may name its repo |

## add_position

```
konjir add_position case=<string> claim=<string> evidence=<[string]>
```

Take the other side of an open case file: your claim and its evidence, seeking the opposite of the opener. A case file holds two positions, one per side; the opener's own person and their agents can't take the other side, and you need Write on a layer of the kolab. Once it has both, a person rules on it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `case` | `string` | yes | The case file's id |
| `claim` | `string` | yes | Your position: the other side, which seeks the opposite of the opener's |
| `evidence` | `[string]` | yes | What backs the claim: kj: addresses (each must resolve), and anything else as text, such as a commit, a file and line, or a test run. At least one. |

## admin_access

```
konjir admin_access actor=<string> kolab=<string>
```

Admin: an actor's access to a kolab: its level and the layers it may write. An agent's is its own grant, cut down to its owner's.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | `string` | yes |  |
| `kolab` | `string` | yes |  |

## admin_add_actor

```
konjir admin_add_actor id=<string> [name=<string>] [owner=<string>]
```

Admin: register a person, or with owner=<account> an agent that a person or an organization owns. Each agent is an actor of its own, with its own sessions and authorship.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes |  |
| `name` | `string` | no |  |
| `owner` | `string` | no | For an agent: the account that owns it, a person or an organization. Omit to register a person, who is also a user account. |

## admin_add_kolab

```
konjir admin_add_kolab name=<string> owner=<string> [title=<string>] [visibility=<public|private|internal>] [base=<read|triage|write|maintain|admin>]
```

Admin: create a kolab owned by a person or an organization. Its name is unique across all of Konjir.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | The short name, unique across all of Konjir: lowercase letters, digits and - |
| `owner` | `string` | yes | The account that owns it: a person or an organization |
| `title` | `string` | no |  |
| `visibility` | `public\|private\|internal` | no | Defaults to private |
| `base` | `read\|triage\|write\|maintain\|admin` | no | An organization's kolab: what every member of the organization holds |

## admin_add_member

```
konjir admin_add_member org=<string> user=<string> [role=<member|owner>]
```

Admin: add a person to an organization, or change their role in it (member or owner).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `string` | yes |  |
| `user` | `string` | yes |  |
| `role` | `member\|owner` | no | owner administers every kolab the organization owns. Defaults to member. |

## admin_add_organization

```
konjir admin_add_organization id=<string> [name=<string>]
```

Admin: register an organization, an account that owns kolabs and agents and has members and teams.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes |  |
| `name` | `string` | no |  |

## admin_add_team

```
konjir admin_add_team org=<string> name=<string> [parent=<string>]
```

Admin: create a team in an organization, optionally under a parent team. Teams hold no konstructs; they are granted access.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `string` | yes |  |
| `name` | `string` | yes |  |
| `parent` | `string` | no | A team of the same organization to nest this one under; its members inherit the parent's access |

## admin_add_team_member

```
konjir admin_add_team_member team=<string> user=<string>
```

Admin: add a member of the team's organization to the team.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `team` | `string` | yes | <org>/<team> |
| `user` | `string` | yes |  |

## admin_apply_ruling

```
konjir admin_apply_ruling ruling=<string> actor=<string> node=<string> [elements=<[{id?,text,parent?,work?}]>] [deltas=<[{kind,element,text?,parent?,work?}]>] [parent=<string>] [unlink=<[{link?,source_element?,target?,kind?}]>]
```

Admin: apply a ruling of Lee's to a node (D47): a new version, written as the actor given, that commits after structural checks only, with no review request, since the ruling is already the approval. With unlink, it also drops links of the node's live version. Its review note records the ruling. It goes through the same per-node commit step as any other commit, so it is rejected as stale if the node moved on meanwhile. Agent sessions can't reach it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ruling` | `string` | yes | The ruling being applied, by its Decisions Log ID, e.g. D46 |
| `actor` | `string` | yes | Who the version is written as, an actor with Write on the node's layer; it writes in the role of that layer |
| `node` | `string` | yes | The node, as <kolab>/<node> (e.g. kolab/kolab-binding), or its name alone when no other kolab has a node of that name |
| `elements` | `[{id?,text,parent?,work?}]` | no |  |
| `deltas` | `[{kind,element,text?,parent?,work?}]` | no |  |
| `parent` | `string` | no | For a variant: the committed parent version, e.g. kj:storefront@2, in the node's kolab |
| `unlink` | `[{link?,source_element?,target?,kind?}]` | no | Links of the node's live version that the ruling drops, so they aren't carried forward, and their open marks settle: [{"source_element":"b1","target":"kj:kolab#R1"}] or [{"link":"<id>"}]; targets in the node's kolab |

## admin_archive

```
konjir admin_archive [kolab=<string>] [organization=<string>] [actor=<string>]
```

Admin: archive a kolab, an organization or an actor, named by exactly one of kolab, organization or actor (D52). It disappears from listings and can't be used: its sessions end and their streams close, no session opens, and nothing in an archived kolab can change. Its data is kept, and its name stays reserved. An organization's kolabs and agents, and a person's agents, are archived with it; a person's own kolabs stay live for their other members. Nothing is deleted; admin_unarchive restores it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kolab` | `string` | no | A kolab, by its name |
| `organization` | `string` | no | An organization: its kolabs and its agents go with it |
| `actor` | `string` | no | A person or an agent: a person's agents go with them; the kolabs a person owns stay live |

## admin_audit

```
konjir admin_audit [kolab=<string>] [subject=<string>] [limit=<int>] [before=<int>]
```

Admin: the audit log (W2.20), newest first, a page at a time (next_before, when given, is the before for the next page): each change that leaves no row of its own to say who made it, with who made it and when. A grant made, changed or removed (grant.set, grant.removed), a person added to or removed from an organization or a team (member.set, member.removed, team_member.added, team_member.removed), an outbox job retried (outbox.retried), a person made or no longer a Konjir admin (admin.granted, admin.revoked), and each admin verb the break-glass token ran (break_glass.used, its subject the verb). Past rows may also say admin.elevated or admin.lowered, which nothing writes now. by is an actor, or admin for the break-glass token. Everything else Kolab writes names who made it on its own row: a node's created_by, a session's opened_by and ended_by, a version's actor and submitted_by, an archive's done_by.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kolab` | `string` | no | Only this kolab's changes: its grants and its outbox jobs |
| `subject` | `string` | no | Only changes to this grantee, person or job |
| `limit` | `int` | no | At most this many, newest first; 100 by default |
| `before` | `int` | no | Only events older than this one: the id of the last event of the previous page, to page back |

## admin_end_session

```
konjir admin_end_session [token=<string>] [session=<string>] [actor=<string>]
```

Admin: end a session, revoking its token. Name it by exactly one of token (kjs_…), session (its 43-character key, as whoami and admin_open_session give it) or actor (every open session it holds: an agent holds one, a person one on each machine they sign in through, D103). Returns the ended session's key (by actor, the first, with all of them in sessions); an error if no open session matched, so a mistyped revoke never passes for one that worked.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `token` | `string` | no | The bearer token the session opened with |
| `session` | `string` | no | The session's key, as whoami gives it: the sha256 of its token, base64url |
| `actor` | `string` | no | The actor whose open sessions to end: an agent's one, or every one a person holds, one on each machine |

```

```

Admin: grant a person, an agent or a team (<org>/<team>) access to a kolab: read, triage, write, maintain or admin, replacing any grant it had there. A write grant names its layers (both by default). An agent can't be granted more than its owner holds. A lower grant narrows the grantee's sessions, and ends any that can no longer reach the kolab.

| `level` | `read\|triage\|write\|maintain\|admin` | yes |  |


Admin: list actors, each with its kind and owner; owner=<account> lists that account's agents. By id. Paged: returns at most limit items (50 by default, at most 200) and next. While next isn't null there are more: call again with cursor=next to read them.

No parameters.

```
konjir admin_open_session actor=<string> role=<product|engineer> [kolab=<string>]
```

Admin: open a session for an actor in one kolab, with one active role. Returns the bearer token the agent connects with, and when it expires: 30 days after it opens, by default (W2.22); an expired token is refused like an ended one. The actor must have access to the kolab; an agent holds its own grant there, never more than its owner.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

| `actor` | `string` | yes |  |

## admin_outbox

```
konjir admin_outbox [state=<pending|dead>] [kolab=<string>] [retry=<string>] [cursor=<string>] [limit=<int>]
```

Admin: the outbox (REV3): the work commits and verdicts still owe, each job with its subject, attempts and last error; kolab=<name> for one kolab's. A rebase job (D43) is a variant to rebase onto its parent's latest version, queued by the parent version named in after; it rebases whatever the variant has live when it runs. A job that fails ten times is dead, and it, and any later cascade of its node, waits until retry=<id> runs it again. Oldest first. Paged: returns at most limit items (50 by default, at most 200) and next. While next isn't null there are more: call again with cursor=next to read them.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `pending\|dead` | no | Only jobs in this state: dead ones wait for an admin to retry them |
| `kolab` | `string` | no | Only jobs of this kolab |
| `retry` | `string` | no | The id of a dead job, or one waiting out its backoff, to run again now |
| `cursor` | `string` | no | The next a previous call returned, to read the page after it, with the same other parameters. Omit it for the first page. |
| `limit` | `int` | no | How many to return: 50 by default, at most 200. |

## annotate

```
konjir annotate address=<string> note=<string> [from=<string>]
```

Leave a note on an address for the layer that owns it: an interpretation you are proceeding on, an assumption, a risk, or something you could not check. It blocks nothing. The owner sees it beside the element in konjir_read_node and in its konjir_list_queries, and can reply. If you need a decision before you can proceed, use konjir_ask instead.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | `string` | yes | A Konjir address, e.g. kj:checkout@3#R1 or kj:checkout#R1~q({"exact":"30 seconds"}): the short form, a node in your kolab. kj:<kolab>/<node>… names the kolab too (kj:shop/checkout@3#R1). Omit @version to use the latest committed version. |
| `note` | `string` | yes | At most 4000 characters |
| `from` | `string` | no | Your own element the note is about |

## answer_query

```
konjir answer_query query=<string> answer=<string> [cites=<[string]>]
```

Answer an open question, or reply to a note, that your layer owns. If the answer settles or changes intent, also amend the spec element: the answer reaches only the asker, the amendment reaches everyone who depends on it. An agent answers a question on the functional layer only by citing what it rests on (cites: committed element addresses or ruling ids), never from its own judgment, and not at all where the kolab's policy keeps those answers for a person (AUT4): with nothing to cite, leave the question open for a person. Anyone may cite. One an answer job handed to a person (waiting_on: "person") is a person's alone to answer.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | `string` | yes |  |
| `answer` | `string` | yes | At most 4000 characters |
| `cites` | `[string]` | no | What the answer rests on, each checked to exist and be readable: committed element addresses (kj:checkout@3#R1, or kj:<kolab>/… in another kolab you read; without @version, the latest committed) and ruling ids (konjir_list_rulings). At most 20. An agent answering a question on the functional layer must cite (AUT4), and at least one cite must be something other than the element the question asks about: with nothing to cite, leave it for a person. |

## archive_agent

```
konjir archive_agent [label=<string>] [agent=<string>]
```

For a person's own session only: archive an agent of yours, <you>-<label> by label=<label>, or by agent=<name> one of yours whose name doesn't start <you>- (konjir_list_agents gives each one's archive_with). Its sessions end, and it no longer counts toward the 10 live agents a person may have. Its name stays its own; an admin may unarchive it. Anything but a live agent of yours is refused alike. An agent's session and the admin token are refused.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | no | The agent's label: archives <you>-<label>. |
| `agent` | `string` | no | The agent's whole name, for an agent of yours whose name doesn't start <you>- (konjir_list_agents gives each one's archive_with). Give label or agent, not both. |

## archive_repository

```
konjir archive_repository repo=<string>
```

For a person with Maintain or Admin in your kolab, never an agent: archive a repository (by URL or id). No new evidence names it, and a binding it implemented may name another; its evidence keeps naming it. Audited.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repo` | `string` | yes | The repository, by its URL or id |

## ask

```
konjir ask address=<string> question=<string> [from=<string>]
```

Ask a question about an address. It routes to the layer that owns the answer: ask a functional spec about intent, a binding about implementation choices. The address may name a committed version or one in review (kj:checkout@2#R4), never a draft; without @version it names the latest committed version. A question about a version in review stays on it when it commits; if it is abandoned or returned to its author instead, the question moves to the latest committed version if the element is there, or is withdrawn, saying why. Quote the words you mean with ~q(...). Set from to the element you wrote pending the answer. You and your owner's other agents (or, for a person, you and your agents) raise at most 60 questions and notes an hour between you; an organization's agents share 300: put several points in one question.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | `string` | yes | A Konjir address, e.g. kj:checkout@3#R1 or kj:checkout#R1~q({"exact":"30 seconds"}): the short form, a node in your kolab. kj:<kolab>/<node>… names the kolab too (kj:shop/checkout@3#R1). Omit @version to use the latest committed version. |
| `question` | `string` | yes | At most 4000 characters |
| `from` | `string` | no | Your own element that waits on this, e.g. kj:checkout-pg@1#b3 (drafts allowed). When the question is answered, that element gets a query_answered mark. |

## clear_mark

```
konjir clear_mark mark=<string>
```

Clear a dirty mark on your layer after checking that your work still holds against the new upstream. Re-pins the dependency and clears what it caused. On a work package with work (In progress, In review or Done), clearing its mark says the work still holds: it keeps its state, recorded as confirmed; if it no longer holds, reopen it instead (konjir_reopen_work). A link into another kolab can be cleared only by someone who reads that kolab, who then holds the link; clearing an access_lost mark is how someone who reads it takes the link or fork over.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mark` | `string` | yes |  |

## create_agent

```
konjir create_agent label=<string>
```

For a person's own session only: make, or find again, an agent of yours, <you>-<label>, for a harness to sign in as (konjir connect sets agents up on Kolab's setup page instead, several at once). An agent of yours already called that is reused. A person has at most 10 live agents (konjir_list_agents lists yours, least recently used named in the refusal at the cap; konjir_archive_agent frees a place), and makes at most 3 in 10 minutes. A name that isn't free to you is refused, whoever holds it. It grants nothing: the agent reaches a kolab once you choose it on Kolab's sign-in page there, with no more access than you hold, at most Write. An agent's session and the admin token are refused.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | yes | The agent's label: up to 24 lowercase letters, digits and '-'. The agent is named <you>-<label>, e.g. ann-product. |

## create_node

```
konjir create_node kind=<spec|prototype|binding|plan> title=<string> [id=<string>] [parent=<string>]
```

Create a node in your kolab. Its kind is fixed, and fixes its layer: spec and prototype are functional; binding is technical. A kolab holds exactly one spec, so a variant of a spec lives in another kolab, as a fork. Create the spec first: each binding names the spec it binds (parent, set once), and its links serve its own spec. A binding holds its own work: its work packages are its elements with a work field. The plan kind is retired (D104): creating a plan is refused. Its name (id) is unique in your kolab; other kolabs may use the same one.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `spec\|prototype\|binding\|plan` | yes | spec: the kolab's one spec (a kolab holds exactly one). prototype: a working representation of the spec, its elements the screens or states, each linked by equivalence to the requirements it shows. binding: how the spec is built on one stack, its decisions and its work packages (elements with a work field); it names the spec. plan is retired (D104): work is planned in the binding, and no plan is made |
| `title` | `string` | yes |  |
| `id` | `string` | no | Readable stable name, unique in your kolab, e.g. checkout: its address is kj:checkout, or kj:<kolab>/checkout from anywhere. Defaults to a ULID. Set once: no verb renames a node. |
| `parent` | `string` | no | The node this one names as its parent, set once and never changed (D78): for a binding, the spec it binds (the default: your kolab's one spec). A spec and a prototype take none. |

## draft

```
konjir draft node=<string> [elements=<[{id?,text,parent?,work?}]>] [deltas=<[{kind,element,text?,parent?,work?}]>] [parent=<string>] [links=<[{source_element?,element?,target,kind?}]>] [unlink=<[{link?,source_element?,target?,kind?}]>]
```

Draft a new version. To change a few elements, send only deltas: [{"kind":"override","element":"R2","text":"new text"}], plus add/remove; everything else carries over, so you never need to copy the whole node. Deltas apply to the latest committed version, never to a draft or a version sent back for changes: after changes are requested on a node's first version, send the full element list again. Or send the full element list and Kolab computes the delta. A binding's elements are its decisions and its work packages: a work package is an element with work fields, {"id":"W1.2","text":"Build the cancel endpoint.","work":{"done_when":"…","depends_on":["W1.1"],"size":"M"}} ("work":{} for one whose fields are still to come); an element without is a decision, and is never work. A milestone has "milestone":true, depends on its members, may carry a target_date and a done_when (its members' exit criterion), and has no size and no links: it has no work of its own. Work left out of an element or a delta keeps its own; "work":null clears it, making the element a decision. Like any binding element, a work package serves spec elements and relies on the binding's decisions through dependency links at element scope (links); it never links another work package: name it in depends_on. Submitting a binding version checks its work fields first (PLN2): Depends on names work packages of the same version, without cycles; only a milestone carries a target date, and a milestone carries no size. Then it is reviewed like any binding version. A job splits a package too big for one job by drafting child packages and making the parent depend on them, or a milestone over them (PLN20). A draft is not truth until konjir_submit_for_review commits it. A version holds at most 1000 elements and 512 KiB of text, each element at most 8000 characters; a larger draft is refused, saying which limit it hit. You and your owner's other agents (or, for a person, you and your agents) draft at most 120 versions an hour between you; an organization's agents share 600. A draft counts when it is made, whoever submits it and whatever becomes of it: put several changes in one draft.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node` | `string` | yes | A node in your kolab, by name (checkout), or <kolab>/<node>. |
| `elements` | `[{id?,text,parent?,work?}]` | no |  |
| `deltas` | `[{kind,element,text?,parent?,work?}]` | no |  |
| `parent` | `string` | no | For a new variant: the parent spec version to inherit from, e.g. kj:storefront@2, or kj:<kolab>/<node>@2 to fork a committed version of another kolab you can read. |
| `links` | `[{source_element?,element?,target,kind?}]` | no | Links to declare from this draft's elements, in the same call: [{"source_element":"b1","target":"kj:spec#R1"}]. Links on earlier versions carry forward automatically. |
| `unlink` | `[{link?,source_element?,target?,kind?}]` | no | Links of the version this draft is built on that it drops, so its commit doesn't carry them forward: [{"source_element":"b1","target":"kj:spec#R1"}] or [{"link":"<id>"}]. Removing a link settles its open mark when the version commits; it is reviewed with the rest of the draft. |

## end_job

```
konjir end_job job=<string> outcome=<done|stopped|failed> [note=<string>]
```

End a job you took, once its agent has exited (done or failed) or you stopped it: its agent's session ends; a build's work package, if its agent still holds it In progress, goes back to To do, released with your note; a review request Kolab gave a reviewing agent that gave no verdict is withdrawn. The ledger records how it ended: when the agent did its item, submitted (a package, a redraft of a marked node, or a binding version serving a spec element), reviewed, answered (a question or note) or cleared (a mark); else released (for a question, mark or spec element, handed to a person, your note saying what they must decide) or stopped. Only the session that took the job.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job` | `string` | yes | The job's id, as konjir_take_job gave it |
| `outcome` | `done\|stopped\|failed` | yes | done: the agent finished and exited; stopped: you stopped it; failed: the agent failed or crashed |
| `note` | `string` | no | What happened, for the ledger and for whoever takes its item next. At most 4000 characters |

## end_session

```
konjir end_session session=<string>
```

For a person's own session only: end one of your open sessions, named by its id from konjir_list_sessions or its first 8 or more characters, matching exactly one. A signed-in one's sign-in is revoked, so it renews no more; either way it ends at once, its listen streams close, and the jobs it ran stop. Ending this session signs you out here. Your other sessions go on. Anything but an open session of yours is refused alike. An agent's session and the admin token are refused.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session` | `string` | yes | The session's id as konjir_list_sessions gives it, or at least its first 8 characters |

## import

```
konjir import file=<object> [dry_run=<boolean>] [update=<boolean>]
```

For a person's own session only, never an agent's or a job's (konjir import <file.json> sends it): import from one file what your session's role may write, into your session's kolab, as you: as product, the spec and the rulings on it; as engineer, the binding (decisions and work packages, with done-when, depends-on and what each serves and relies on), the rulings on it and the repository. A whole file takes two passes, two sign-ins, in either order; what the other pass writes is reported as other_pass, naming the sign-in, and complete is true only once the whole file is in. The whole file is checked before anything is written. Each write is its verb's own: konjir_create_node, konjir_draft and konjir_submit_for_review (the kolab's policy decides whether a version commits unreviewed or waits in review, VER11), konjir_rule's checks, with the ruling's ID and the date it was given (dated rulings are audited, and keep when they were recorded), and konjir_register_repository. You need Write on the layer of your role and, for a repository, Maintain. Run again, it changes nothing that is there and equal, reports what differs without overwriting it (update=true drafts the file's version of a node of your pass that differs), and completes what a run before it left waiting or unfinished. dry_run=true writes nothing and says what it would do. A version a reviewer sent back is reported with their note (sent_back) and never resubmitted by itself. The result lists each step: created, unchanged, differs, in_review, waiting, other_pass, sent_back or failed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | `object` | yes | The import file, as one JSON object: {"format": "konjir-import/1", "kolab": …, "spec": …, "binding": …, "rulings": […], "repository": …}. README.md, "Importing a kolab", gives its shape |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | true: check the file and say what the import would write, writing nothing |
| `update` | `boolean` | no | true: a node of your pass whose latest committed version differs from the file gets the file's as a new version, reviewed as any is, dropping links the file doesn't give; refused if it would drop a work package with work. Without it, a difference is reported and left alone |

## instructions

```
konjir instructions [which=<operating|reviewer|playbook>] [kind=<build|review|answer|mark|serve>]
```

Call before your first change: the full operating instructions for working through Konjir, with your kolab's precedent (rulings, resolved overrides and answered questions) so settled questions are not re-litigated. With which=reviewer, call before reviewing: how to review a version that waits for you, and how to give your verdict with konjir_review. Without which=playbook, returns the same text as the konjir_operating_instructions and konjir_reviewer_instructions prompts. With which=playbook and a kind, the playbook a job of that kind follows (JOB7): server text with no prompt of its own, the item's specifics as placeholders.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `which` | `operating\|reviewer\|playbook` | no | operating (the default): the rules, with your kolab's precedent, rulings and answered questions. reviewer: how to review a version that waits for you. playbook: the playbook for the kind of job item kind names. |
| `kind` | `build\|review\|answer\|mark\|serve` | no | With which=playbook: the kind of job item, one of build, review, answer, mark, serve. Its playbook says what done is, which verbs do it and when to hand the item to a person, and gives the text a job of that kind is told, with the item's specifics as placeholders (JOB7). |

## lineage

```
konjir lineage node=<string> direction=<upstream|downstream> [version=<int>] [cursor=<string>] [limit=<int>]
```

Walk lineage from a node version (the latest committed one, or version): upstream = what it depends on, each link's source element and the address it pins, kj:<node>@<version>#<element> (what to konjir_resolve when reviewing it); downstream = what depends on it. By link id. A link into a kolab you can't read shows only that it exists: target is null, with target_hidden. Paged: returns at most limit items (50 by default, at most 200) and next. While next isn't null there are more: call again with cursor=next to read them.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node` | `string` | yes | A node in your kolab, by name (checkout), or <kolab>/<node>. |
| `version` | `int` | no | With direction=upstream only: the version to walk from, e.g. one waiting for your review, whose links are the ones it was drafted with. Defaults to the latest committed version. |
| `direction` | `upstream\|downstream` | yes | Required. upstream = what this node relies on; downstream = what relies on it. |
| `cursor` | `string` | no | The next a previous call returned, to read the page after it, with the same other parameters. Omit it for the first page. |
| `limit` | `int` | no | How many to return: 50 by default, at most 200. |

## link

```
konjir link kind=<dependency|derivation|equivalence> source=<string> target=<string> [source_element=<string>]
```

Declare that one of your elements relies on an address, so you are told when it changes. Name your element either in source (kj:checkout-pg@2#b1) or in source_element; a link without a source element makes your whole version, and everything downstream of it, dirty on any change. kind: dependency (usual), derivation (generated from it), equivalence (must stay in sync). Linking two elements of the same spec is allowed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `dependency\|derivation\|equivalence` | yes | dependency = relies on; derivation = generated from; equivalence = must stay in sync |
| `source` | `string` | yes | Your element, e.g. kj:checkout-pg@2#b1 (drafts allowed). |
| `source_element` | `string` | no | Alternative to putting #element in source. |
| `target` | `string` | yes | What it relies on; must be committed and resolve exactly. e.g. kj:checkout@3#R1, or kj:<kolab>/<node>… in another kolab you can read (the link rests on your Read there, and is marked access_lost if that goes), or a span: kj:checkout#R1~q({"exact":"30 seconds","prefix":"Checkout completes within","suffix":"of payment confirming"}). For a span, quote only the few words you rely on (at most 1,000 characters), and give several whole words either side as prefix and suffix, not one word: they must still surround the quote in the target. |

## open_case

```
konjir open_case address=<string> question=<string> claim=<string> seeks=<change_intent|keep_intent> evidence=<[string]>
```

Open a case file: a disagreement about one element that you and the other side could not settle between yourselves, such as a requirement that code reality says can't be met as written. Give the question in dispute and your position: a claim, its evidence, and the side it takes (seeks keep_intent or change_intent). Only those with Write on a layer of the kolab may. It waits in the inbox of the element's layer for the other side's position (konjir_add_position) and then a person's ruling (konjir_rule). Work under way goes on meanwhile, but until it is ruled no one can pull a work package that serves or relies on its element. Ask first (konjir_ask) when the element is unclear: most questions need an answer, not a ruling. When building shows the spec can't be met as written, open one against the spec element with your evidence (commits, file and line, test runs), and never patch the behavior instead.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | `string` | yes | The element in dispute, e.g. kj:checkout#R1, on a committed version in your kolab |
| `question` | `string` | yes | What the two sides disagree on, in one sentence |
| `claim` | `string` | yes | Your position |
| `seeks` | `change_intent\|keep_intent` | yes | The side your position takes: keep_intent (the element stands as written) or change_intent (it must change). The other side takes the opposite. |
| `evidence` | `[string]` | yes | What backs the claim: kj: addresses (each must resolve), and anything else as text, such as a commit, a file and line, or a test run. At least one. |

## pull_work

```
konjir pull_work [binding=<string>] [plan=<string>]
```

Pull work: Kolab gives you the first ready work package of your kolab's binding in natural ID order (never a decision, nor a milestone), makes it In progress for you with a lease (30 minutes unless the kolab sets another), and returns its context and the git trailer to put in each commit for it (Konjir-Work: kj:<kolab>/<binding>#<id>). Every tool call you make to Kolab renews the lease, but konjir_whoami and reading your inbox or answers, which your channel does by itself; if you make none for its length, the package goes back to To do and you are told in your answers. You hold one work package In progress at a time, in any kolab: finish or release it before pulling another. From an engineer session that may write the technical layer. binding is needed only when more than one binding of your kolab has work packages. If a package is too big for one job, split it (PLN20): draft child packages in the binding, make it depend on them, and release it. With nothing ready, it says why (blocked by dependencies, questions or case files). A pull counts as a draft against your hourly budget.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `binding` | `string` | no | The binding to pull from: needed only when more than one binding of your kolab has work packages |
| `plan` | `string` | no | Retired (D104): use binding |

## read_node

```
konjir read_node node=<string> [version=<int>] [cursor=<string>]
```

Read the elements of a node version, with who wrote it and who made the node, each with its address, the questions and notes raised on it (open and answered, from any version: the newest 20, with more_questions counting the rest), the rulings on it, which are precedent, and its open case files; a binding's work packages show their work fields (work), and its decisions have none. Defaults to the latest committed version. The node is one of your kolab's, or <kolab>/<node> in any kolab you can read. For a variant of your kolab whose parent committed a newer version, rebase says its rebase is queued: Kolab rebases it in the background, and a new version of it appears once that is done. A version holds at most 1000 elements; a read returns 250 of them at a time, in order, and next is null once it has returned the last. While next isn't null, read again with cursor=next for the rest.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node` | `string` | yes | A node by name: one in your kolab (checkout), or <kolab>/<node> in any kolab you can read. |
| `version` | `int` | no |  |
| `cursor` | `string` | no | A version holds at most 1000 elements, read 250 at a time: pass the next a read returned for the elements after them. Omit it for the first. |

## read_policy

```
konjir read_policy
```

For a person with Admin in your kolab, from their own session (never an agent's): its autonomy policy, how far agents act there without a person (AUT1). Who approves functional versions (approve_functional), technical versions (approve_technical) and work packages (approve_work); whether a binding version also needs a product approval (product_review_of_bindings, VER13); who answers a question on the functional layer (answer_functional); and the job caps (jobs_per_person, jobs_per_kolab), never above the server's own limits. With which settings differ from the defaults, and who changed it last. Rulings and registering a repository are always a person's, whatever it says (AUT5).

No parameters.

```
konjir read_work work=<string> [events_cursor=<string>] [limit=<int>]
```

Read one work package of your kolab, kj:<binding>#<id>: where it stands, why it is blocked, its fields (done_when, depends_on with their states, size), its elements: each spec element it serves and each decision of its binding it relies on, at its latest committed version, with that element's links (a decision's spec elements, with their ancestors), questions, notes and rulings; the git trailer for its commits (and former_trailers, those its commits carried while it was a plan's, before D104), its open_marks, at_risk and revisit (the repository, commit SHAs, files and pull requests of its work since it was last To do) while an open mark on it says something it serves or relies on changed (PLN10), and its events (who changed its state, when, against which versions), oldest first. A package its binding removed, or made a decision, reads too, with removed_in. Events are paged: while events_next isn't null, call again with events_cursor=events_next.

| `events_cursor` | `string` | no | The events_next a previous read returned, for the events after it |

With Maintain or Admin in your kolab: give a work package that is To do or In progress to `to`, who must hold Write on the technical layer there and hold no work package In progress. It becomes In progress for them, with a fresh lease, and both are told in their answers. Not a milestone, nor a package its binding removed.

## record_release

```
konjir record_release work=<string> run=<string> sha=<string> [repo=<string>] [title=<string>]
```

Record the release of a work package, kj:<binding>#<id>, after its approval and then the deploy that released it, by someone with Write on the technical layer other than its assignee, from an engineer session outside any job (a job never merges or deploys, JOB4): the deploy run, a GitHub Actions run of the package's registered repository (<repository URL>/actions/runs/<id>), and the commit it released, by its full 40-hex sha. Only on a package whose work field says release: true, In review and approved, waiting for its release: the approval comes first, and this makes it Done (PLN16). Refused before the approval, on any other package, from its assignee, and from a job's session. Kolab can't check the run or the sha against GitHub: they are your word. A release confirms no repository. In a shell, konjir work deliver <work> --release <run> records it from the checkout, with HEAD as the released commit unless --commit names another. Counts as a draft against your hourly budget.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `work` | `string` | yes | A work package of your kolab: kj:<binding>#<id>, e.g. kj:checkout-binding#W1.2. An address from before D104, kj:<plan>#<id>, names the package where it moved |
| `run` | `string` | yes | The deploy run that released the work: a GitHub Actions run of the package's repository, by its link, <repository URL>/actions/runs/<id> (such as https://github.com/acme/orders/actions/runs/123). At most 2000 characters |
| `sha` | `string` | yes | The commit it released, by its full sha: 40 hexadecimal characters |
| `repo` | `string` | no | The released commit's repository: the URL of one registered in your kolab. Leave it out to use the package's own (its repo, or its binding's implementation) |
| `title` | `string` | no | A summary of the release ("deployed to production"). At most 4000 characters |

## register_repository

```
konjir register_repository url=<string> root_sha=<string> [binding=<string>]
```

For a person with Maintain or Admin in your kolab, never an agent (your session's kolab only: for another kolab, sign in there first, konjir login --kolab <kolab>): register the git repository work is done in (KON7), by its https URL and its root commit (the parentless commit, `git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD`), and, with binding, as that binding's implementation (one per binding). Kolab never reads git: the root commit pins which checkout `konjir work deliver` accepts, and the repository counts as confirmed once a work package that cites it is approved by someone other than you and the package's assignee. Audited. konjir repo register, run in a checkout, works both out for you.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | `string` | yes | The repository's https URL, such as https://github.com/acme/orders: no user, password, query or fragment. Kolab stores it lower-cased in the host, without a trailing slash or .git |
| `root_sha` | `string` | yes | Its root commit: the full sha `git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD` prints in a checkout of it. Every delivery from a checkout is checked against it |
| `binding` | `string` | no | The binding this repository implements, one repository per binding: its work packages are done here unless one names another repo |

```
konjir release_work work=<string> [note=<string>]
```

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `note` | `string` | no | Why, for whoever pulls it next. At most 4000 characters |

The agent's own calls renew it too. Only the session that took the job; refused once the job has ended or its lease has lapsed (its item then went back to the queue).

```
konjir reopen_work work=<string> note=<string>
```

Open new work on a Done work package, kj:<binding>#<id>, from an engineer session with Write on the technical layer: it returns to To do under the same id, for anyone to pull, with its history and evidence kept and your note recorded. Use it when a package is at risk (something it serves or relies on changed since it was done) and the work no longer holds; if the work still holds, clear its mark instead (konjir_clear_mark), which keeps it Done. Its open marks that the new work answers settle with it. Not a milestone, which is Done when its members are.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `work` | `string` | yes | A work package of your kolab: kj:<binding>#<id>, e.g. kj:checkout-binding#W1.2. An address from before D104, kj:<plan>#<id>, names the package where it moved |
| `note` | `string` | yes | Why the work is opened again. At most 4000 characters |

## resolve

```
konjir resolve address=<string>
```

Resolve an address to its current content: kj:<node>… in your kolab, or kj:<kolab>/<node>… in any kolab you can read. Use this instead of caching spec text. Status is ok, fuzzy or orphan. For a quoted span: ok means the exact words, with the prefix or suffix you quoted still around them (or no prefix or suffix was quoted). fuzzy means the span changed: either its wording was edited, or the exact words now appear only without their quoted context, such as a copy in another statement. Both kinds of fuzzy mark whatever links to the span (fuzzy_reanchor). orphan means it is gone.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | `string` | yes | A Konjir address, e.g. kj:checkout@3#R1 or kj:checkout#R1~q({"exact":"30 seconds"}): the short form, a node in your kolab. kj:<kolab>/<node>… names the kolab too (kj:shop/checkout@3#R1). Omit @version to use the latest committed version. |

## resolve_override

```
konjir resolve_override mark=<string> resolution=<reaffirm|adopt_parent|amend> [text=<string>]
```

Resolve a stale or orphaned override in a variant spec: reaffirm (keep yours), adopt_parent (take the parent text), or amend (new text). Becomes precedent for the same situation elsewhere. The resolution is a new version, so it counts as one of your drafts in the hour.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mark` | `string` | yes |  |
| `resolution` | `reaffirm\|adopt_parent\|amend` | yes |  |
| `text` | `string` | no |  |

## review

```
konjir review verdict=<approve|request_changes> [node=<string>] [version=<int>] [work=<string>] [note=<string>] [findings=<[{kind,elements,explanation}]>]
```

Record your verdict on a version in review that you did not write, on your own layer (node and version), or on a work package In review that you are not the assignee of (work, from an engineer session with Write on the technical layer): approve, or request_changes with a note (and, for a version, findings). For a work package, read it first with konjir_read_work, and check its evidence (commits, pull requests, test runs) against its done-when with your own access to the repository, outside Kolab: approve makes it Done, or, for one that must be released (release: true), leaves it In review, approved, until its release is recorded (konjir_record_release), so approve it on everything else and never request changes for its being unreleased; request_changes returns it to its assignee, In progress. Review requests for you are in your inbox (konjir_list_reviews). Read a version first with konjir_read_node. Report a contradiction (two elements that cannot both hold, or a binding element that conflicts with a requirement it links to: stricter, looser or different) only with request_changes. A layer_leak is content in the wrong layer that conflicts with nothing (implementation in a spec, or behavior a binding adds that its linked requirements don't mention); it can come with approve: the version commits and a question goes to the layer that owns the answer. Anything that conflicts is a contradiction. Send compound requirements back to be split. konjir_instructions which=reviewer has the full checklist.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node` | `string` | no | The node of the version to review, with version. Leave out for a work package (work). |
| `version` | `int` | no |  |
| `work` | `string` | no | A work package In review to review instead of a version: kj:<binding>#<id>, e.g. kj:checkout-binding#W1.2 |
| `verdict` | `approve\|request_changes` | yes | For a version: approve commits it (one approval is enough); request_changes returns it to its author as a draft. For a work package: approve makes it Done; request_changes returns it to its assignee, In progress |
| `note` | `string` | no | What you checked, or what must change, and what you ran and only read. Required with request_changes. |
| `findings` | `[{kind,elements,explanation}]` | no |  |

## rule

```
konjir rule text=<string> [case=<string>] [address=<string>] [effect=<change_intent|keep_intent>] [verdicts=<object>] [replaces=<string>] [ref=<string>]
```

Rule, as a person (never an agent), from a session in the role that writes the element's layer, holding Write on it. With case: rule on that case file, sustaining exactly one of its two positions and overruling the other; the ruling's effect is the side the sustained one seeks. You may not rule on one you or your agent holds a position on. With address and no case: rule directly, with no case file behind it. A direct ruling says whether it changes the intent or keeps it and asks for another way, and supersedes any case file still open on its element. A ruling that changes the intent marks the element, with a question to its layer, until a version amends it. A ruling records its author and date, never changes, and is served to every agent in the kolab as precedent; a later ruling says what it replaces.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `case` | `string` | no | The case file to rule on. Omit it, and give address, to rule directly. |
| `address` | `string` | no | For a ruling with no case file behind it: the element or node it rules on, e.g. kj:checkout#R1 |
| `text` | `string` | yes | The ruling, as agents will be served it as precedent |
| `effect` | `change_intent\|keep_intent` | no | Required for a direct ruling. change_intent: the intent changes, and the element is marked until it is amended. keep_intent: the intent stands; find another way to meet it as written. On a case file it is the side of the position you sustain, and may be left out. |
| `verdicts` | `object` | no | With case: each position's verdict, by position id, sustaining exactly one: {"<position>":"sustained","<position>":"overruled"} |
| `replaces` | `string` | no | What this ruling overrules, in words, if anything |
| `ref` | `string` | no | The ruling's own name in your kolab, such as D109: a letter, then up to 39 letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-', unique in the kolab and never changed. Its precedent line names it |

## set_policy

```
konjir set_policy [approve_functional=<agent|person|other_person>] [approve_technical=<agent|person|other_person>] [approve_work=<agent|person>] [product_review_of_bindings=<boolean>] [answer_functional=<agent_cited|person>] [jobs_per_person=<int>] [jobs_per_kolab=<int>]
```

For a person with Admin in your kolab, from their own session (never an agent's): change settings of its autonomy policy (AUT1). Name only the settings to change; the rest keep their values. The defaults: a person approves functional versions; an agent may approve technical versions and work packages; no product approval of bindings; an agent answers a functional question only citing committed elements or rulings; at most 4 jobs a person and 8 a kolab. Takes effect at once: review requests waiting in the kolab are given again under the new policy (those it no longer allows are withdrawn, those it newly allows are asked). Audited with you as its actor. Your session's kolab only: for another kolab, sign in there first (konjir login --kolab <kolab>).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `approve_functional` | `agent\|person\|other_person` | no | Who approves functional versions (AUT2): person (the default), other_person (a person other than the one whose intent the version carries: its author, or its author's owner), or agent (any reviewer with Write on the layer) |
| `approve_technical` | `agent\|person\|other_person` | no | Who approves technical versions (AUT2): agent (the default: any reviewer with Write on the layer), person, or other_person |
| `approve_work` | `agent\|person` | no | Who approves work packages (AUT3): agent (the default) or person |
| `product_review_of_bindings` | `boolean` | no | Whether a binding version also needs a product approval, from a product session, that it doesn't change behavior (VER13): false by default |
| `answer_functional` | `agent_cited\|person` | no | Who answers a question on the functional layer (AUT4): agent_cited (the default: an agent too, citing the committed elements or rulings its answer rests on) or person |
| `jobs_per_person` | `int` | no | How many jobs a person runs at once in this kolab (AUT7): 1 to 4, the server's own limit (4 by default) |
| `jobs_per_kolab` | `int` | no | How many jobs this kolab runs at once (AUT7): 1 to 8, the server's own limit (8 by default) |

## set_work_lease

```
konjir set_work_lease minutes=<int>
```

With Maintain or Admin in your kolab: how long a lease on work In progress lasts there, in minutes, from 1 to 1440 (30 by default). Audited. Leases running now keep their time; the next pull or renewal takes the new length. Your session's kolab only: for another kolab, sign in there first (konjir login --kolab <kolab>).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `minutes` | `int` | yes | From 1 to 1440 |

## submit_for_review

```
konjir submit_for_review node=<string> version=<int>
```

Submit a draft. Kolab runs its structural checks; if they fail, the draft stays drafted, with the reason. If they pass, the version goes into review, and commits once another actor who holds Write on its layer approves (konjir_review). The review request reaches only those who can review that layer in the role they work in: a person, or an agent signed in with the role that writes the layer (or not signed in there); reviewers lists them, and if it is empty, review says who to bring in. If no one else holds Write on the layer, the checks alone commit it, and it is recorded as unreviewed. A binding version's work packages pass their work checks (PLN2) before it goes into review. The result names the version that committed or waits (a stale draft may be folded into a rebase). Resubmit a draft that came back with changes requested the same way; resubmitting a version still in review asks whoever can review it now, and commits it unreviewed if no one else holds Write on its layer any more.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node` | `string` | yes | A node in your kolab, by name (checkout), or <kolab>/<node>. |
| `version` | `int` | yes |  |

## submit_work

```
konjir submit_work work=<string> [evidence=<[{kind,sha?,pr?,url?,title?,summary?,files?,repo?}]>] [note=<string>]
```

Submit the work package you hold In progress, kj:<binding>#<id>, for review, once it meets its done-when: it needs at least one commit or pull request among its evidence (give them here, as konjir_add_evidence takes them, or before); test runs are optional. It goes In review, with a review request to each other actor with Write on the technical layer, and you hold it no longer, so you can pull another. If no one else holds Write on the technical layer, it is Done on submission, recorded as unreviewed. The verdict comes back in your answers: approved (Done; or, for a package whose work field says release: true, approved and waiting In review until its release is recorded with konjir_record_release after the deploy, by someone other than you, outside any job), or changes requested (In progress for you again, with a fresh lease, even if you have pulled another meanwhile). Submitting a package that waits in review asks whoever can review it now. Counts as a draft against your hourly budget. Refused once your lease has lapsed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `work` | `string` | yes | A work package of your kolab: kj:<binding>#<id>, e.g. kj:checkout-binding#W1.2. An address from before D104, kj:<plan>#<id>, names the package where it moved |
| `evidence` | `[{kind,sha?,pr?,url?,title?,summary?,files?,repo?}]` | no | Evidence to record with the submission, as konjir_add_evidence takes it |
| `note` | `string` | no | What you did, for the reviewer. At most 4000 characters |

## take_job

```
konjir take_job machine=<string> [kinds=<[build|review|answer|mark|serve]>]
```

For a person's own session with Write on the technical layer, never an agent's: take the next item in your kolab and start a job on it for one of your pool agents (<you>-engineer-<n>), which `konjir work` runs as one headless agent and which stops after that item. First a work package returned with changes requested to a free agent of yours, resumed as that agent; then a work package In review or a technical version in review that an agent of yours may review (never its author); then the first ready work package, pulled for the agent as konjir_pull_work pulls; then, for a runner that names them in kinds, an open question or note people raised on a technical node (answer), then an open mark on one (mark), each oldest first, and then a spec element no binding element serves (serve). Questions, notes and marks on the functional layer stay with people. An item whose last two jobs ended in the last hour without doing it is held back; a question, mark or spec element once its last job did, as a hand-off does: the agent leaves it, its last words, the job's note, saying what the person must decide. Kolab picks a free pool agent, making one on first need (within the 10 live agents a person may have), grants it what you hold here (at most Write), and opens its session, its only one. The result carries that session's token, shown this once: hand it to the agent and nowhere else; it ends with the job, or when your session ends. Also the job's id, its kind (build, review, answer, mark or serve), its item, the agent, the lease (renew it with konjir_renew_job), the agent's instructions (its kind's playbook, konjir_instructions which=playbook, filled in with the item, then your kolab's precedent), and now, Kolab's clock. A review is offered only where the kolab's policy lets an agent approve it. At most 4 live jobs a person and 8 a kolab, or fewer where the kolab's policy says so (AUT7). With nothing to take, or past a cap, taken is false and why says why.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `machine` | `string` | yes | A label for the machine the job runs on, 1 to 64 characters, such as lee-laptop: it names the machine in the ledger |
| `kinds` | `[build\|review\|answer\|mark\|serve]` | no | The kinds of item your runner can run, any of build, review, answer, mark, serve: build and review if you name none, so a runner that knows no other kind is never given one (JOB6) |

## unlink

```
konjir unlink node=<string> version=<int> links=<[{link?,source_element?,target?,kind?}]>
```

Remove links in a draft of yours, so its commit doesn't carry them forward: a link you no longer rely on, or an orphaned one whose target is gone (re-point it by linking the replacement, then remove the old one). Name each by its id (konjir_lineage, konjir_list_stale) or by its source element and target; a link into a kolab you can't read only by its id, and its target shows as null, with target_hidden. The removal is part of the draft: it is reviewed with it, and the links and their open marks settle only when it commits. A link the draft declared itself goes at once. Linking the same link again in the draft takes the removal back.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node` | `string` | yes | A node in your kolab, by name (checkout), or <kolab>/<node>. |
| `version` | `int` | yes | Your draft of the node: the removal is part of it, reviewed with it |
| `links` | `[{link?,source_element?,target?,kind?}]` | yes | The links to remove: [{"link":"<id>"}], or [{"source_element":"b1","target":"kj:spec#R1"}] |

## whoami

```
konjir whoami
```

Show the actor, role and layer your session token carries (an agent also names the account that owns it), the kolab it works in and your access there, and the resources to subscribe to for pushed updates: your layer's inbox and your answers, both in that kolab. A session can subscribe only to its own kolab's. session is the session's key, the sha256 of its token: Kolab never shows the token again after it is issued.

No parameters.
